newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTR-Australia's NSW sees A$27 mln 97/98 surplus.
newsitem.headline: RTR-Australia's NSW sees A$27 mln 97/98 surplus.

text.p: New South Wales (NSW), Australia's most populous state, on Tuesday projected an underlying budget surplus of A$27 million for the 1997/98 fiscal year to June 30.
This compares with a predicted A$67 million underlying surplus for the 1996/97 year and forecast surpluses of A$36 million for 1998/99 and A$195 million for 1999/00.

In his budget speech, New South Wales Treasurer Michael Egan said it was the first time consecutive underlying budget surpluses had been delivered, and the 1997/98 forecast would be only the third such surplus in the state's history.
"This budget will ensure we have a sound and strengthening financial position," Egan told parliament.
On a headline basis the 1997/98 budget projected a deficit of A$56 million.
But Egan said that if the government gets approval to sell the state-owned betting agency, the Totaliser Agency Board (TAB), the headline budget surplus in 1997/98 would be around A$1.5 billion.
Carry over costs associated with the sale of the former State Bank of NSW accounted formost of the difference between the underlying and headline results, NSW Treasury officials said.
For 1996/97, the headline balance is forecast to be a surplus of A$119 million.

The underlying budget position excludes extraordinary items from equity restructures and the sale of government business enterprises. The headline result incorporates all transactions of the budget sector.
Not including the possible TAB sale, the government forecast assest sales of A$322 million in 1997/98, down from A$364 million in 1996/97.
The budget papers forecast that receipts would increase by 5.7 percent in 1997/98, a real increase of 4.1 percent.
Current outlays were projected to rise by 4.2 percent in 1997/98 (two percent in real terms), while capital outlays would rise 24.2 percent (21.6 percent in real terms).
The capital outlays reflected the expenditures on the Olympic and Homebush Bay projects and the continuation of the major infrastructure renewal program for the State Rail Authority.
Egan said 1997/98 would be the peak year for capital expenditure on the Olympics, and forecast it at A$628 million.
